source.title: Developmental emergence of hippocampal fast-field "ripple" oscillations in the behaving rat pup

confidence_rationale: This is the original, classical demonstration that hippocampal ripple oscillations -- the fast-field signature associated with replay -- are ABSENT during the first postnatal week despite sharp waves themselves being present, and only begin to emerge at the end of the second postnatal week (day 12-20), tracking the developmental GABA-A switch from excitatory to inhibitory signaling. This is the founding empirical result behind DEV-NEED-029 ('replay hardware maturation gate') and the direct historical ancestor of the more recent, more mechanistically detailed Pochinok (2024) and Noguchi (2023) papers in this same directory -- it establishes the phenomenon those later causal/intracellular studies go on to explain mechanistically.
failure_signatures: This is freely-behaving-rat-pup extracellular recording without causal manipulation -- it is a purely observational/correlational demonstration of the developmental timeline (ripples absent early, present later, tracking GABA switch timing), not a causal test of the inhibition-maturation mechanism; that causal test is supplied by the companion Pochinok (2024) entry.

The paper notes the developmental timeline 'may also reflect hitherto unidentified emergence of neuronal gap junctions' -- the authors themselves flag GABA-switch timing as A candidate explanation, not a proven sole cause, at the time of writing (later confirmed more directly causal by Pochinok 2024).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Recording from freely behaving rat pups aged postnatal day 12-20 (with wire tetrodes) and head-fixed pups (with silicon probes), the authors show that while sharp-wave-associated hippocampal unit bursts are present from the first postnatal week, the fast-field RIPPLE oscillation component does not begin to emerge until the end of the second postnatal week, increasing gradually until around day 18, after which the intra-ripple frequency reaches adult values. This developmental timeline parallels the GABA-A receptor-mediated signaling switch from excitatory to inhibitory.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-533 requires that offline-processing competence, including the basic capacity to generate replay-supporting ripple events, has its own developmental trajectory distinct from mere offline-window occurrence. Buhl & Buzsaki is the classical, founding demonstration of exactly this: ripples -- as opposed to the cruder sharp-wave events that precede them -- are simply ABSENT for the first postnatal week and emerge gradually over the second, tracking a specific developmental switch in inhibitory signaling. This is the historical anchor for DEV-NEED-029's 'replay hardware maturation gate,' later given a causal mechanistic account by Pochinok et al. (2024, this same directory) and a finer-grained sequence-fidelity extension by Noguchi et al. (2023, this same directory).
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is purely observational (no causal manipulation of the inhibitory mechanism), so while it establishes the developmental timeline and correlates it with GABA-switch timing, it does not itself prove inhibition maturation CAUSES ripple emergence -- that causal step is supplied by the companion Pochinok (2024) entry, which post-dates this paper by nearly two decades and uses optogenetic/chemogenetic tools unavailable in 2005.
mapping.source_context: Rat; postnatal days 12-20; wire tetrode recording in freely behaving pups and silicon-probe recording in head-fixed pups; extracellular local field potential and multi-unit recording, no causal manipulation.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality: the classical, foundational, widely-cited demonstration of ripple developmental emergence, co-authored by a leading figure in hippocampal oscillation research. Mapping fidelity moderate-good: directly establishes the phenomenon MECH-533's hardware-maturation sub-claim needs, though the causal mechanism (vs. correlation with GABA-switch timing) is only established by the later Pochinok (2024) work in this same directory.
